title: Tidebone Crossing
description: Six tapered, eroded limestone ribs arc in sequence above flared buttress roots and a small paved passage.

review.notes: Round 1 of the new budget, judged against the PR #6 round-3 notes. Fixed: the outlines are smooth now, with no stair-stepping and no hammerhead caps. New problems: the ribs no longer close into arches; they are six free-standing tusks in a row, each ending in a blunt rounded hook, so it reads as a row of tusks or claws, not a rib arch (hero.jpg, turn_200). Fix: pair the ribs so opposite ribs meet or overlap overhead as closed or nearly closed arches, as in the plan, and give the free ends a broken fracture face instead of a rounded knob. Root bodies: still smooth, soft drapery-like flares with vertical folds, like melted wax or cloth, not stone (closeup_base). Fix: a buttressed foot with hard fractured planes and a few large stone blocks set into the turf. Material: each rib changes tone abruptly at hard horizontal seam lines (beige above, blue-grey below), and the round dark pocks repeat along every rib (closeup_upper). Fix: one continuous ivory limestone with weathering graded towards the foot, no hard colour seams, varied pitting. Scale: at 80 m the figure is a dot in the hero; frame the hero closer, with the figure at a rib foot.
